job.style: a conversation between a teacher and two students

response.passage: Teacher: Today, let’s talk about how our bodies change with exercise. Rahul, why do you think your legs ache the day after a long run? Rahul: I think it is because lactic acid has built up and stayed in my legs. Teacher: Actually, that is a common myth. Soreness happens because of tiny tears in muscle fibers that occur during exercise, which then repair and grow stronger while you rest. Priya: So, does that mean my muscles grow while I am lifting weights at the gym? Teacher: Not exactly. Muscles actually grow during the recovery period after your workout, not while you are pushing the weights. Priya: My brother says he only does sit-ups to lose his belly fat. Is that how it works? Teacher: No, Priya. You cannot choose to burn fat from just one specific area of your body. When you exercise, your body burns fat from all over. Also, remember that sweating is just your body’s way of cooling down, not a measure of how much fat you have burned. Finally, always remember to cool down by walking slowly after a run instead of sitting down immediately, as this helps your heart rate return to normal safely.
response.summary: Exercise causes tiny muscle tears that lead to growth during rest, not during the workout itself. Fat loss occurs across the whole body rather than in specific spots, and sweating is simply a cooling mechanism.
